samples.summary: DOCX import recurses into nested tables with no depth cap, and the model it produces then flows into uncapped recursive consumers (text/markdown serializers, DOCX exporter) — the layout cap the diff adds is the only producer-independent bound
samples.evidence: `DocxImporter.convertTable` calls itself for every `<w:tbl>` inside a cell (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:415) with no `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` check, so a crafted .docx overflows the stack during import — before any layout runs. If it survives import, the resulting >32-deep `TableData` is walked by uncapped recursions outside the layout: `packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts:60/76/87` (`blockToText`→`tableToText`→`cellToText`→`blockToText`, used by clipboard `text/plain`) and `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:202` (`blockToXml`→`tableToXml`→`blockToXml`). `packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:145` explicitly justifies its own cap by "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)"; that same argument applies to the importer and to these serializers, which the change leaves unbounded.

samples.summary: The truncating reader's output can be written back to the CRDT, making the read-time truncation a permanent deletion of rows below the cap
samples.evidence: `setHeader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:903-911) and `setFooter` (:942-950) take `this.getDocument()` — the document produced by the now-capped `treeNodeToBlock` (:466-484), where a table at depth ≥ MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH reads as `rows: []` — and, on the treeless fallback path, hand it to `writeFullDocument`, which rebuilds every node via `buildBlockNode` (:3221). `setDocument` (:986-996) has the same shape. The reader's 'degrade, do not vanish' promise only holds for reads; any round-trip through these writers persists the truncation into the shared tree, so the content 'nobody can then open to repair' becomes content nobody can repair at all. Fix belongs on the write path (refuse to rewrite a truncated table, or mark truncated tables so writers skip them).

samples.summary: Backend nesting ceiling is a second, independently-declared copy of the same 32 with different inclusive/exclusive semantics — content the API accepts is now silently truncated by both readers
samples.evidence: `const MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:806) with `if (depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH) throw` (:443) bounds the same table-in-cell recursion the new `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32` bounds, but the backend rejects only at *greater than* 32 while `treeNodeToBlock` truncates at *>= 32* (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). A `PUT /content` payload at the backend's limit therefore validates, persists, and then reads back with its innermost table emptied on every client. Since `@wafflebase/docs` now exports the constant (packages/docs/src/index.ts:97, node.ts:145) and the backend already imports from it (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:36), the two ceilings can and will drift.

samples.summary: A third, shallower nesting cap (paste, depth 8) now coexists with the new shared 32 — a legally-deep document copies out and pastes back with its inner tables dropped
samples.evidence: `const MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` in packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:71, enforced in `sanitizeTableData` (:308), is a fourth-hand copy of the same 'how deep may tables nest' policy the change centralises in `model/table-nesting.ts`. With the reader and layout now admitting 32 levels, a 9-deep table that renders fine is silently flattened on copy/paste. Not broken by this diff, but it is now the outlier that will drift from the exported constant; either express it as `Math.min(..., MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)` or document why paste is deliberately stricter.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `DocxImporter.convertTable` is declared with only `(tblEl, imageUrls)` at packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:246-249 and self-recurses per nested `<w:tbl>` at :415 with no depth parameter or cap anywhere on that path (entry calls at :135 and :743 likewise pass two args). The consumers named are also genuinely uncapped: serialize/text.ts recurses blockToText(:60)→tableToText(:73/76)→cellToText(:80/87)→blockToText with no depth argument in the file, and export/docx-exporter.ts recurses blockToXml(:201-202)→tableToXml(:258)→blockToXml(:355). Searching wide for any other bound: MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH (model/table-nesting.ts:26) is consumed only by the CRDT reader (model/crdt-tree.ts:225) and the layout (view/table-layout.ts:145); MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH (model/numeric-attrs.ts:408) bounds only the numeric-banding walk and does not truncate the model passed downstream; and clipboard's MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8 (view/clipboard.ts:71,308) guards the *paste* producer — the other producer named in table-layout.ts:139-140 — which makes the DOCX importer's omission the concrete gap, not a hypothetical one. Two of the reviewer's sub-claims are inaccurate: the Markdown serializer does not recurse (serialize/markdown.ts:203-205 emits a `[nested table]` placeholder), and the CLI import wraps throws into InvalidDocxError (packages/cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:73-81). Neither is a counterexample to the claim under test, because the importer's own unbounded recursion and the two truly recursive consumers remain, and the CLI export path reaches DocxExporter on stored content that never passes the CRDT reader's cap. In lane for blast-radius: the diff's new structural guard has producer paths reaching the same recursion around it, at the very producer its own comment names. Major, not critical: the reachable outcome is a stack overflow / failed import or export, not silent data loss or a permission bypass.

finding.summary: The truncating reader's output can be written back to the CRDT, making the read-time truncation a permanent deletion of rows below the cap
finding.evidence: `setHeader` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:903-911) and `setFooter` (:942-950) take `this.getDocument()` — the document produced by the now-capped `treeNodeToBlock` (:466-484), where a table at depth ≥ MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH reads as `rows: []` — and, on the treeless fallback path, hand it to `writeFullDocument`, which rebuilds every node via `buildBlockNode` (:3221). `setDocument` (:986-996) has the same shape. The reader's 'degrade, do not vanish' promise only holds for reads; any round-trip through these writers persists the truncation into the shared tree, so the content 'nobody can then open to repair' becomes content nobody can repair at all. verdict.reason: The read-time cap exists as described (yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484; twin crdt-tree.ts:224-229), and the finding's core claim — the truncating reader's output can be written back through buildBlockNode/buildCellNode, making truncation permanent — is real, though NOT at the sites the reviewer cited. Corrections: (a) setDocument (:986-996) writes a caller-supplied doc, not getDocument()'s output; its production caller passes a parsed DOCX import (docs-view.tsx:396). (b) setHeader (:903-915) / setFooter (:942-954) reach writeFullDocument only in the branch guarded by `!tree || typeof tree.getRootTreeNode !== 'function'`; in that same condition getDocument() (:806-812) returns `{blocks: []}` without calling treeNodeToBlock, and ensureTree (docs-view.tsx:59-97) creates the Tree before the store is used, so no tree-derived truncation can flow there. However, the same round-trip IS reachable on ordinary paths in the same file: updateBlock rebuilds a whole block subtree via buildBlockNode (:1680) from a read-model block, reached by paste-into-table (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4743 -> updateBlockDirect -> store.updateBlock); and updateTableCell rebuilds a cell via buildCellNode (:2815) from read-model cells in mergeCells (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1114) and splitCell (:1143). A table nested at/below MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH reads as `rows: []`, is rebuilt from that model, and the truncation is persisted into the CRDT — data loss on a write path, in the blast-radius lane (reader behaviour change whose write-side consumers were not considered). Since the fix the finding proposes belongs on the write path and that write path really does persist the truncation, refuting would drop a real defect on a citation technicality.

finding.summary: Revision-preview snapshot path recurses over the raw tree before `docsTreeToDocument`'s new nesting cap can apply
finding.evidence: `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (packages/frontend/src/components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143, recursive call at :140) walks the whole parsed snapshot tree with no depth bound and only then hands the result to `docsTreeToDocument` (:178), which is the reader the PR bounded with `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). A `block > row > cell > block > table > …` chain written by a peer — precisely the hazard `model/table-nesting.ts:11` says no attribute band can reach — therefore overflows the stack in this pre-pass and throws a `RangeError` out of `parseDocsSnapshot`, so the version-history preview still crashes on the document the cap was added to keep openable. The cap protects the live store (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:480`) and the engine reader but not this consumer; the fix is a depth bound in `normalizeYsonTreeNode`. I could not confirm how deep a tree the server-stored snapshots can actually carry, hence low confidence, but the path is reachable from the preview UI.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. `normalizeYsonTreeNode` (snapshot-adapters.ts:123-143) recurses over every child of the parsed snapshot tree at :140 with no depth parameter or bound, and `parseDocsSnapshot` runs it as a full pre-pass at :178 before handing the result to `docsTreeToDocument`, which is where the PR's cap lives (crdt-tree.ts:219-229, `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`; mirrored in the live store at yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484). The repo's own rationale (table-nesting.ts:5-17) states the hazard is reachable by ordinary peer Tree writes at arbitrary depth, so the preview consumer walks the unbounded structure first and the cap never gets a chance to truncate it. I checked for an upstream bound and found none: `unwrapYsonScalars` returns `Tree` aggregates by reference (unwrap-yson.ts:97-98) and so never descends into the tree, and the path is reachable from the UI (revision-preview.tsx:88, effect at :197-228). The only mitigating factor is the try/catch at revision-preview.tsx:212-221, which turns the RangeError into an error banner rather than an app crash — that softens the reviewer's "crashes" wording but does not make the site safe: the revision preview still cannot render the document the cap was added to keep openable. A guard whose invariant is defeated at another entry point outside the diff is in this lens's lane, so I have no named ground to refute on.

finding.summary: New read-side nesting cap has no matching write-side cap: a truncated table written back prunes the peer's deeper rows from the CRDT
finding.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` now reads a table nested past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `rows: []` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:483, crdt-tree.ts:228), but the in-memory `Block` produced that way is the same object the write path serializes back: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1680) does `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))`, replacing the whole block subtree with what `buildBlockNode` (line 364/375) derives from `block.tableData.rows`. Any `doc.updateBlockDirect(...)` on an ancestor table (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185, 4743) therefore rewrites the truncated shape into the tree and permanently deletes everything below level 32 for every peer. The backend writer has the same shape (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200). Truncation-on-read is recoverable; truncation written back is not.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The read-side cap exists (yorkie-doc-store.ts:479-484; crdt-tree.ts:224-229) and yields rows: [] for tables nested past MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH. That truncated Block is the same object the editor holds: getDocument()/treeToDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:802-823, 548) feeds Document._document (document.ts:129,148) and Document.getBlock (document.ts:226-240). The write path has no matching cap and no merge: updateBlock replaces the entire block node with buildBlockNode(block) (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1670-1680), whose table branch serializes exactly block.tableData.rows (364-376). Two reachable callers outside the diff pass an ancestor table block straight back: text-editor.ts:4171-4185 (cell-range clear) and 4721-4743 (paste into cell), both via Document.updateBlockDirect (document.ts:765-768). The ancestor table still lays out and is editable — the layout cap (table-layout.ts:145) only blanks the deep descendant — so editing it rewrites the truncated shape into the CRDT and permanently removes the below-cap subtree for every peer. No guard elsewhere prevents a >32-deep chain existing, since the cap's own rationale is that a peer can write such depth with ordinary Tree writes. In-lane (reader contract change with an unupdated writer consumer) and blocking at major (irrecoverable data loss on a reachable path).

finding.summary: DOCX import recurses into nested tables with no depth cap, so the producer the layout comment names can still overflow the stack and can create documents deeper than the reader will ever show
finding.evidence: `table-layout.ts`'s new comment says the layout bounds itself because "the layout takes documents from other producers too (DOCX import, paste)". That producer is `DocxImporter.convertTable`, which recurses unbounded at packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:415 (`cellBlocks.push(DocxImporter.convertTable(childEl, imageUrls))`) — a crafted .docx overflows the stack during import, before any layout runs, so the layout cap never sees it. A merely deep (say 40-level) import also succeeds, is written into the CRDT by the uncapped `buildBlockNode` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:375), and is then silently truncated to 32 on the next read. No cap exists on any producer side.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence claim directly. `DocxImporter.convertTable` is declared with only (tblEl, imageUrls) at packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:246 and recurses on nested <w:tbl> at :415 with no depth argument; a grep of that whole file for depth/limit/MAX/nest yields only unrelated direct-child-walk comments, and docx-parser.ts has no depth logic either. The import result reaches the CRDT through docx-actions.ts:31 -> pending-imports -> docs-view.tsx:396 / apply-imported-content.ts:226 -> YorkieDocStore.setDocument -> writeFullDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3221) -> buildBlockNode/buildCellNode (yorkie-doc-store.ts:364/400), none of which carry or enforce a depth. The new cap (table-nesting.ts:26) is enforced only on read (crdt-tree.ts:225, yorkie-doc-store.ts:480) and in layout (table-layout.ts:145), whose comment at :139-140 explicitly names DOCX import as a producer it does not trust. Candidate counterexamples were checked and do not apply: numeric-attrs.ts:111 MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH bounds only bandBlockNumerics' own walk (:408) and is not on the docs import path, and backend assertValidBlock/MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH (docs-content.controller.ts:443) guards the REST content API, which the browser import bypasses by writing directly to Yorkie and which cannot stop an overflow inside convertTable itself. So a crafted deep .docx overflows the stack during import, and a merely deep (e.g. 40-level) one is written whole and then silently truncated to 32 on the next read — a real blast-radius consequence at untouched producer sites.

finding.summary: Sibling clamp on the model path still spreads row widths (`Math.max(0, ...rows.map(...))`) — the exact RangeError the new normalizeCellRange comment says it folded to avoid
finding.evidence: `normalizeCellRange` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts) now folds with `reduce` because "`Math.max(...rows)` throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments, and the row count is a peer's to choose". The same computation on the model path was not changed: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 does `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`. verdict.reason: The claimed code is present verbatim: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 computes `Math.max(0, ...rows.map((row) => row.cells.length)) - 1`, spreading one argument per table row, while the diff's sibling computation at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:136-137 was deliberately converted to a `reduce` fold with the comment that `Math.max(...rows)` throws RangeError past ~100k arguments "and the row count is a peer's to choose". No row-count band exists anywhere: packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts caps columns (MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS=256 at :95, applied :256 and :380), spans (:213-219) and nesting depth (:111), but `bandOneBlock` iterates `table.rows` at :383-412 with no length cap, so `rows.length` is peer-controlled and unbounded.
